chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Yaqteen from his brother al-Husayn from Ali ibn Yaqteen who said:

I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about passing through Medina during the outward journey (to Mecca) — is it better, or during the return journey? He said, 'There is no harm in that, whichever it is.'

key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: there is no harm / it is permissible

ai.seo_question: Is it better to pass through Medina on the way to Mecca or on the way back during Hajj?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this narration from Imam al-Rida (AS) resolves a specific fiqh query regarding the ritual merit of traversing Medina during Hajj. The Imam’s response, 'there is no harm in that, whichever it is,' establishes that the outward and return passages are equally valid, removing any obligatory preference for one over the other in this context. This ruling highlights the Shia emphasis on ease and the absence of unnecessary ritual burden in travel-related acts of worship.
